header.instrument: Capital Allowances Act 2001, plant and machinery writing down allowances; the pool rates and the annual investment allowance as published in HMRC's Capital Allowances Manual and the CA guidance on GOV.UK
header.coverage: The two writing-down pools and the annual investment allowance only. NOT bundled: the first-year allowance and full-expensing rules, the structures and buildings allowance, the small pools allowance, the car CO2 emission thresholds that decide which pool a car enters, and every balancing-charge computation. Those are date-sensitive and could not be stated with confidence in this build, so no row claims them.
header.note: A UK writing down allowance is a reducing-balance allowance on a POOL of expenditure, not an asset-by-asset depreciation charge. This server applies the pool rate to a single asset so a figure can be produced per asset; the tax computation is still made on the pool. The rate is a maximum: a business may claim less.

rates.note: Most plant and machinery: computers, office equipment, machinery, vans, and cars in the main pool.
Integral features of a building, long-life assets, thermal insulation, solar panels, and higher-emission cars. Which cars fall here depends on CO2 thresholds that are not bundled.

AIA is a 100 percent first-year deduction on qualifying plant and machinery, capped at GBP 1,000,000 of expenditure per 12-month period and shared across a group. Cars never qualify. Expenditure covered by AIA does not then enter a pool. This row exists so an asset can be marked as fully relieved in year one; it is not a depreciation rate.
